articles/homeservers.html.title: Homeservers | Uniform STUN Server
articles/homeservers.html.summary: Homeservers A Matrix homeserver hands its users time-limited TURN credentials, made with a secret it shares with the TURN server. Give both the same secret: Turn:SharedSecrets here, separated by commas when there are several, e.g. while replacing one. Synapse In homeserver.yaml: turn_uris: - "turn:turn.example.org:3478?transport=udp" - "turn:turn.example.org:3478?transport=tcp" turn_shared_secret: "a-long-random-secret" turn_user_lifetime: 86400000 Uniform Chat Server Uniform Chat Server has this server built in, see its guide. To use a separate one instead, set Calls:TurnUris and Calls:TurnSharedSecret: { "Calls": { "TurnUris": "turn:turn.example.org:3478?transport=udp,turn:turn.example.org:3478?transport=tcp", "TurnSharedSecret": "a-long-random-secret" } } Without a homeserver Fixed users work for other software, as name:password pairs in Turn:Users. Anyone with such a password can use the relay until you remove it, so prefer time-limited credentials.

articles/running.html.title: Running | Uniform STUN Server
articles/running.html.summary: Running Ports The server must be reachable from the internet on these ports. Behind a home router, forward them to the server's computer: Port Protocol Use 3478 UDP and TCP STUN and TURN, Turn:Port 49152–65535 UDP Relayed calls, Turn:MinRelayPort to Turn:MaxRelayPort; each call uses one or two 5349, if set TCP TURN over TLS, Turn:TlsPort Install Unpack the release anywhere. On Debian and Ubuntu, the releases are also an apt repository, for x64 and arm64: add it once, with its signing key, then install the server, which sudo apt upgrade keeps up to date. The command is then uniform-stun-server in place of ./uniform-stun-server below. sudo install -d -m 0755 /etc/apt/keyrings curl -fsSL https://github.com/tagcode/Uniform.Chat/releases/latest/download/uniform-chat-archive-keyring.gpg | sudo tee /etc/apt/keyrings/uniform-chat.gpg > /dev/null echo "deb [signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/uniform-chat.gpg] https://github.com/tagcode/Uniform.Chat/releases/ latest/download/" | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/uniform-chat.list sudo apt update sudo apt install uniform-stun-server First start Give the server its public address and a shared secret. Put the secret in the settings file or an environment variable, not on the command line, where other users of the computer can see it: export Turn__SharedSecrets='a-long-random-secret' ./uniform-stun-server --Turn:ExternalAddress=203.0.113.5 --Turn:Realm=example.org Turn:ExternalAddress is the public address peers send relayed calls to: the router's public address when the server is behind NAT. When it changes now and then, e.g. on a home connection, give a dynamic DNS name instead, which is resolved again every minute, or stun:host:port of a STUN server, which is asked every minute. Relays made after a change get the new address. The log tells where it listens: TURN server listening on udp 0.0.0.0:3478, tcp 0.0.0.0:3478, relaying from 203.0.113.5 ports 49152-65535 When a setting cannot work, the server prints why and stops, e.g. without credentials or without an external address. Settings come from, later ones overriding earlier ones: appsettings.json next to the program ~/.config/uniform-stun-server/settings.json Environment variables, with __ between parts: Turn__Port=3478 The command line: --Turn:Port=3478 Its log files are in ~/.local/share/uniform-stun-server/logs, one per start. As a system service Unpack it in /opt/uniform-stun-server, create a user for it, and write the settings, with the secret, to /etc/uniform-stun-server/settings.json: sudo useradd --system --home-dir /var/lib/uniform-stun-server --shell /usr/sbin/nologin uniform-stun-server sudo mkdir -p /opt/uniform-stun-server /etc/uniform-stun-server sudo tar -xzf uniform-stun-server-<version>-linux-x64.tar.gz -C /opt/uniform-stun-server --strip-components=1 sudo nano /etc/uniform-stun-server/settings.json sudo chown -R uniform-stun-server:uniform-stun-server /etc/uniform-stun-server sudo chmod 600 /etc/uniform-stun-server/settings.json { "Turn": { "Realm": "example.org", "ExternalAddress": "203.0.113.5", "SharedSecrets": "a-long-random-secret" } } Then the unit file /etc/systemd/system/uniform-stun-server.service: [Unit] Description=Uniform STUN and TURN server After=network-online.target Wants=network-online.target [Service] User=uniform-stun-server Group=uniform-stun-server ExecStart=/opt/uniform-stun-server/uniform-stun-server Environment=XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/etc Environment=XDG_DATA_HOME=/var/lib StateDirectory=uniform-stun-server Restart=on-failure NoNewPrivileges=true ProtectSystem=strict ProtectHome=true PrivateTmp=true ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/uniform-stun-server [Install] WantedBy=multi-user.target sudo systemctl daemon-reload sudo systemctl enable --now uniform-stun-server journalctl -u uniform-stun-server -f For TURN over TLS on port 443, which is below 1024, add AmbientCapabilities=CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE to the [Service] section, and make the certificate readable by the user.

articles/settings.html.title: Settings | Uniform STUN Server
articles/settings.html.summary: Settings All settings are in section Turn. ↻ marks that a change takes effect after a restart; all of them do, as the server binds its ports at start. Option Default Meaning Turn:Enabled false Run the server; this program's appsettings.json sets it to true. ↻ Turn:Realm not set Realm of the credentials, usually your domain; turn when not set. ↻ Turn:ListenAddress 0.0.0.0 Address the TURN server listens on. ↻ Turn:Port 3478 Port of STUN and TURN over UDP and TCP. ↻ Turn:Tcp true Also listen over TCP on that port, for networks that block UDP. ↻ Turn:TlsPort not set Port of TURN over TLS, such as 5349; none when not set. ↻ Turn:CertificatePath not set Certificate file of TURN over TLS, with its intermediate certificates, such as certbot's fullchain.pem; a renewed file is picked up without a restart. ↻ Turn:KeyPath not set Private key of that certificate, such as certbot's privkey.pem. ↻ Turn:ExternalAddress not set Public IPv4 address that relayed data is sent to, the router's public address when the server is behind NAT: a fixed address, a host name that is resolved again at every check, e.g. of a dynamic DNS service, or stun:host:port to ask that STUN server. Needed unless Turn:ListenAddress is that address. A changed address, e.g. after the router's DHCP lease, goes to new relays. ↻ Turn:AddressCheckInterval 00:01:00 How often the server checks its local and public addresses for changes, besides when the system reports one. ↻ Turn:RelayAddress not set Address the relay ports bind; the listen address when not set. ↻ Turn:MinRelayPort 49152 First UDP port of relayed addresses. ↻ Turn:MaxRelayPort 65535 Last UDP port of relayed addresses; behind NAT, forward the whole range. ↻ Turn:MaxAllocations 1000 Most relays at once; a call uses one or two. ↻ Turn:MaxAllocationsPerUser 10 Most relays at once per user. ↻ Turn:AllowedPeers not set Private addresses relayed to anyway, separated by commas, such as 192.168.1.0/24; private, loopback and link-local addresses are refused otherwise, so outsiders cannot reach your network through the server. ↻ Turn:SharedSecrets not set Shared secrets of time-limited credentials, separated by commas, the same as the homeserver's, see Homeservers. Keep them out of command lines. ↻ Turn:Users not set Fixed users as name:password, separated by commas. Keep them out of command lines. ↻ Logging:LogLevel:Default Information Least important log entries written: Debug adds refused credentials.

index.html.title: STUN and TURN server | Uniform STUN Server
index.html.summary: Uniform STUN Server uniform-stun-server is a STUN and TURN server. It relays voice and video calls between people whose networks block direct connections, as on mobile networks and behind strict firewalls. Matrix homeservers such as Synapse hand out its credentials to their users' calls; Uniform Chat Server has the same server built in. Running: ports, first start, and as a service. Settings: every setting. Homeservers: connecting it to Synapse or Uniform Chat Server.
